open_points.subject: A10 effect send authority selection
open_points.text: "Before sending ... the kernel needs one of: an approved, unused EffectApproval ... whose request_digest equals ...; ... When both exist, the approval is used and recorded as the authority."
open_points.question: If more than one approved, unused approval for the same run/node/element matches the same request_digest, which approval record must be consumed and marked `used`?
options: Use the oldest matching approval (lowest store order)
Use the newest matching approval (highest store order)
Refuse send as ambiguous and require a new approval

open_points.subject: A10 fresh approval after `not_applied`
open_points.text: "A fresh approval after `not_applied` is one requested after that resolution; approvals recorded before it never count."
open_points.question: What is the exact cutoff when there are multiple `not_applied` resolutions for the same element (or an approval requested before resolution but decided after)? Which approvals are valid for the resend?
options: Only approvals with `requested_at` after the latest `not_applied` resolution are valid
Link approvals explicitly to a specific EffectAttempt number and require a post-resolution link
Invalidate all prior approvals at resolution time and force exactly one new request
open_points.default_guess: Treat the latest `not_applied` resolution as the cutoff and require `requested_at` after it.

open_points.subject: A08/A09 manifest instance address validity
open_points.text: A08 rule 5 checks only that an instance "has `api_base_url`"; A09 rule 6 later refers to "the instance or its address is missing or not allowed" without defining full syntax validity checks for `api_base_url`.
open_points.question: If `api_base_url` is present but syntactically invalid/unparseable, must proposal/accept fail as manifest mismatch, or is this only a send-time `operation_failed` pre-send failure?
options: Allow binding, fail at send time with `operation_failed` detail
Treat as kernel start-time configuration error
open_points.default_guess: Allow binding and fail at send time as pre-send `operation_failed` (address invalid).

open_points.subject: A20 vs A09 failure_detail encoding
open_points.text: A20: "`failure_detail` ... is cut to `failure_detail_bytes_max` at a UTF-8 character boundary." A09: "The body of an error response is not interpreted; at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it is kept as `failure_detail`."
open_points.question: How must `failure_detail` be produced when the captured error body bytes are not valid UTF-8?
options: Decode as UTF-8 with replacement, then truncate at character boundary
Store raw bytes and truncate by bytes (despite UTF-8 rule)
Drop body text and store only a fixed marker/length
open_points.default_guess: Decode with UTF-8 replacement and then truncate at a UTF-8 character boundary.
